blocks.prompt: 4. Find the equation of lines represented by \(x^{2} + 2xy\sec\alpha + y^{2} = 0\) and also find measure of the angle between them. (Problems 1-5)
blocks.explanation:
Yeh bhi homogeneous second degree equation hai, lekin is ke beech wale coefficient mein \(\sec\alpha\) jaisa letter hai.
Aise mein middle term split karna mushkil hai, kyunke poore numbers nahi milte.
Is liye Theorem 8 ki tayyar lines \(by + x(h \pm \sqrt{h^{2}-ab}) = 0\) istemal karenge.
Trigonometry ki identity \(\sec^{2}\alpha - 1 = \tan^{2}\alpha\) square root ko saaf kar degi.
Plan: \(a\), \(h\), \(b\); square root; lines; angle; aakhir mein slopes ka jama aur product se tasdeeq.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(x^{2} + 2xy\sec\alpha + y^{2} = 0\).
Maloom karna: dono lines aur un ke darmiyan angle.
Tareeqa: Theorem 8 se lines \(by + x(h \pm \sqrt{h^{2}-ab}) = 0\), aur Section 5.9 se \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{2\sqrt{h^{2}-ab}}{a + b}\). Hum \(\alpha\) ko acute angle (\(0 < \alpha < 90^{\circ}\)) maan rahe hain, taa ke \(\tan\alpha\) positive ho aur \(\sqrt{\tan^{2}\alpha} = \tan\alpha\) likh sakein.

\(a\), \(h\), \(b\) parhein
\[a = 1,\quad 2h = 2\sec\alpha \Rightarrow h = \sec\alpha,\quad b = 1\]
Kyun: \(xy\) ka coefficient \(2\sec\alpha\) hai, us ka aadha \(\sec\alpha\). Yahan 2 pehle se likha hua hai, is liye \(h\) saaf nazar aa raha hai.

Square root ko saaf karein
\[h^{2} - ab = \sec^{2}\alpha - 1 = \tan^{2}\alpha\]
\[\sqrt{h^{2} - ab} = \tan\alpha\]
Kyun: identity \(1 + \tan^{2}\alpha = \sec^{2}\alpha\) se \(\sec^{2}\alpha - 1 = \tan^{2}\alpha\). Aur \(\tan^{2}\alpha\) kabhi negative nahi hota, is liye yeh lines hamesha real hain, \(\alpha\) jo bhi ho.

Dono lines likhein
\[y + x(\sec\alpha + \tan\alpha) = 0\]
\[y + x(\sec\alpha - \tan\alpha) = 0\]
Kyun: formula \(by + x(h \pm \sqrt{h^{2}-ab}) = 0\) mein \(b = 1\), \(h = \sec\alpha\) aur root \(= \tan\alpha\) rakh diya. Plus se ek line, minus se doosri.

\(y\) ke liye hal karein
\[y = -(\sec\alpha + \tan\alpha)x\]
\[y = -(\sec\alpha - \tan\alpha)x\]
\[\text{yani } y = x(-\sec\alpha \pm \tan\alpha)\]
Kyun: \(x\) wala term doosri taraf le gaye to sign badal gaya.
Dhyan dein: minus sign \(\sec\alpha\) ke saath hai, \(\tan\alpha\) ke saath \(\pm\). Isi jagah answer key ghalti kar gayi hai (neeche dekhiye).

Lines ke darmiyan angle
\[\tan\theta = \dfrac{2\tan\alpha}{1 + 1} = \tan\alpha\]
\[\theta = \alpha\]
Kyun: formula (iv) mein \(a + b = 2\) aur numerator \(2\tan\alpha\); 2 cancel. Jab do angles ke tan barabar hon (aur dono acute hon) to angles bhi barabar. Aam \(\alpha\) ke liye acute angle ka \(\tan\theta = |\tan\alpha|\) hai.

Tasdeeq:
\[m_{1}m_{2} = (\sec\alpha + \tan\alpha)(\sec\alpha - \tan\alpha)\]
\[= \sec^{2}\alpha - \tan^{2}\alpha = 1 = \dfrac{a}{b} \;\checkmark\]
\[m_{1} + m_{2} = -2\sec\alpha = -\dfrac{2h}{b} \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: slopes ka jama aur product dono Section 5.9 ke formulas se mil gaye. Product 1 hai, \(-1\) nahi, is liye lines perpendicular NAHI hain.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Answer key (number 4) mein \(y = x(\tan\alpha \pm \sec\alpha)\) aur \(90^{\circ}\) likha hai. Dono ghalat hain. Un slopes ka product \(\tan^{2}\alpha - \sec^{2}\alpha = -1\) banta hai aur un ki joint equation \(y^{2} - 2xy\tan\alpha - x^{2} = 0\) banti hai, jo di gayi equation nahi. Di gayi equation mein \(a + b = 2 \ne 0\), is liye lines perpendicular ho hi nahi saktin. Sahi jawab: \(y = x(-\sec\alpha \pm \tan\alpha)\) aur angle \(\theta = \alpha\).
